title: Canadian Overnight Repo Rate Average
summary: The Bank of Canada publishes daily CORRA transparency data showing overnight repo rates ranging from 2.27% to 2.33% for March 24-30, 2026. The page provides full transparency metrics including trimmed volume, percentile distributions (5th, 25th, 75th, 95th), number of data submitters (14-15), and the CORRA Compounded Index values. CORRA measures the cost of overnight general collateral CAD funding using Government of Canada securities as collateral.
key_points: CORRA values for March 24–30, 2026 ranged from 2.27% to 2.33%, hovering around the 2.30% level
Total daily dollar trading volume eligible for CORRA ranged from $47.5B to $57.4B during the reporting period
Trimmed dollar volume (after removing outliers) ranged from $35.6B to $43.1B, with trimming rate consistently at 2.25%
Number of unique data submitters ranged from 14 to 15 per day
CORRA Compounded Index stood at approximately 115.97–115.98 as of March 27–31, 2026, with base value of 100 on June 12, 2020
Data published daily between 9:00 and 11:00 ET; transparency metrics include mean and mode values alongside raw rates
why_it_matters: CORRA is Canada's designated risk-free rate and reference benchmark for floating rate notes, loans, and financial derivatives. The transparency metrics (trimmed volume, percentile distributions, participant counts) provide insight into the health and liquidity of Canada's overnight repo market. This data supports market structure analysis but does not constitute a macro catalyst or policy signal.
macro_context: CORRA operates independently from Bank of Canada policy rate decisions. This page presents historical transparency data only—no current policy signals, rate guidance, or macro commentary. The 2.27-2.33% range during March 24-30, 2026 suggests stable overnight funding conditions but cannot be interpreted as a market-moving event without additional context.
market_structure_context: CORRA is Canada's benchmark overnight repo rate measuring the cost of general collateral funding in CAD. The Bank of Canada provides this as a public good with full transparency on calculation methodology, data submitters, and volume distributions. The 2.27-2.33% range indicates stable overnight funding conditions with 14-15 active market participants. The trimmed volume approach and percentile reporting (5th, 25th, 75th, 95th) provide insight into repo market distribution, outlier handling, and liquidity health in Canada's overnight funding markets.
